description.narrative: Réseau d’Appui aux Initiatives Locales This project aims to contribute to the food sovereignty of communes by improving agricultural yields, by supporting the Communal Innovation Platforms in the rural communes of Matankari, Falwel and Bana, all locatedin the Dosso region. These platforms have been set up by RAIL-Niger, in collaboration with ICRISAT, INRAN and IITA, as part of the “Climate-smart agricultural technologies to improve rural livelihoods and food security in Niger” project (CSAT _Niger). The action we are planning, with the support of PASOC 4 through Lot No. 2 of this Call for Projects, will revitalize these structures and scale them up bycreating a functional network of PCis. This action will be implemented in a difficult natural context,characterized by the underperformance of agro-sylvo-pastoral production systems that are highly dependent on climatic factors: abundant rainfall can trigger double-digit growth rates, while rainfall deficits generally coincide with economic recession. This dependence on climatic factors leadsto very sluggish economic growth and affects its sustainability. The areas currently under cultivation constitute a fragile ecosystem, subject to mining and weakened by water and wind erosion. As the potential for irrigable land is very low (less than 2% of Niger's arable land), it is the current dominant extensive agricultural ecosystems that support the main production systems, exposing theland for a long time to widespread degradation in various forms. The livestock sector has experienced recurrent pastoral crises (e.g. those of 1973 and 1984), which have strongly induced the emergence of new types of actors in the sector, with the gradual shift in ownership of livestock from the traditional herder to the traderand civil servant, keeping some destitute former herders in the position of salaried shepherds. Generally speaking, livestock farming is highly unproductive and does little to meet the basic needs of farming families. In terms of nutrition, malnutrition has become a structural problem due to the poor performance of agro-sylvo-pastoral production systems. It is aggravated by cyclical phenomena, with peaks during the lean season. The main determinant of such a situation is the almost permanent food insecurity of households, combined with the high incidence of childhood illnesses. According to official data, acute malnutrition has affected more than 10% (alert threshold) of children aged 6-59 months in recent years. Malnutrition rates sometimes exceed theemergency threshold of 15%. Prevalence among children aged 6-23 months very often exceeds the emergency threshold. However, RAIL, which intends to support OXFAM and ROTAB in achieving the objectives set out in the implementation of PASOC 4, particularly with regard to the theme of “Support for governance of food security”, is in turn requesting a grant to support the PCIs described above, with a view to improving their performance and disseminating good agroecological practices in the Dosso region, and progressively in the other regions of Niger.

participating-org.narrative: RAIL was set up in 1999 by former Niger employees of AFVP (Association Française des Volontaires du Progrès). These former employees seized the opportunity presented by AFVP's withdrawal from the implementation of projects and programs in Niger to position RAIL as a Nigerien development and decentralization support organization in the emerging context of decentralization. RAIL was recognized as a development NGO on August 18, 2004 by the government of Niger through decree 325/MI/D/DGAPJ/DLP. RAIL has a national base, having intervened in all eight (8) of Niger's regions since 2004. Today, RAIL is still active in six (6) of Niger's regions: Tillabéri, Niamey, Dosso, Tahoua, Zinder and Diffa). RAIL operates in 4 main areas, broken down into 11 axes and 2 cross-cutting axes. Area1: Governance (with 3 axes):Axis 1: Communal project management, inter-communality and decentralized cooperationArea 2: Governance of social and economic infrastructuresArea 3: Peace, security and the fight against violent extremismArea2: Social protection (with 3 axes):Axis 4: Social reintegration and empowerment of vulnerable peopleAxis 5: Emergency and humanitarian actionAxis 6: Migration phenomenonArea 3: Food and nutritional security (with 3 axes) :Axis 7: Management of natural resources in the face of climate changeAxis 8: Promotion of agrosilvopastoral and fisheries value chains and value chainsArea 9: NutritionArea 4: Water, Hygiene and Sanitation (with 2 axes):Axis 10: Access to drinking waterAxis 11: Hygiene practices andsanitation2 Cross-cutting axes : - Institutional, organizational and operational development of the NGO RAIL - Gender and inclusion Vision RAIL aims to be a sustainable development NGO that promotes inclusion and social justice in a world of solidarity,where communities live in dignity and security. Contribute to improving the living conditions of vulnerable populations by reducing poverty and inequality through the promotion of inclusive development and social justice actions.Governing bodies : As a non-governmental organization, RAIL's organizational and institutional structure comprises a General Assembly (GA), a Board of Directors and a Statutory Auditor. The General Assembly brings together all the members of the NGO. It is the supreme body with the broadest powers. It is responsible for defining the broad strategic orientations and general policies of the NGO. It sets up a Board of Directors, which reports annually to the Board on the management of the organization. As for the Board of Directors,it signs agreements with partners and orders the NGO's expenditure, which it may delegate toa permanent secretary to act on its behalf. The Board also implements the decisions, strategic orientations and general policies ofthe NGO defined by the General Meeting. It draws up annual program documents and activity reports, which it submits to the AGM for approval. It is made up of a permanent secretary, an administrative and financial department and an operational department that monitors and provides technical support to the NGO's regional and local coordinations. Network membership: RAIL is an active member of the Platform of Decentralization Organizations, where it holds the position of Treasurer. RAIL is also a member of the Groupement desAides Privées - GAP. RAIL is also a member of a sub-regional security platform comprising the NGO Groupe de Recherche Action en Sciences Humaines-GRASH (Burkina Faso), Action de Recherche pour la Gouvernance Africaine -ARGA (Mali) and Réseau d'Appui aux InitiativesLocales -RAIL (Niger). RAIL's average annual budget is around one billion FCFA.
